records.literal_gloss: You heard that it was said, Not you will commit adultery.

en.L: You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.'
en.B: You have heard the commandment, 'Do not commit adultery.'
en.R: You have heard that the law says, 'Do not commit adultery.' That means do not be unfaithful to your husband or wife.

decisions.choice: You shall not commit adultery: the seventh commandment (Exodus 20:14)
decisions.reason: The command forbade sexual relations with another person's spouse (Deuteronomy 5:18).

decisions.choice: That means do not be unfaithful to your husband or wife.
decisions.reason: Readable says what adultery is.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I but say to you that everyone looking at a woman in order to desire her already committed adultery [with] her in the heart of him.

en.L: But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
en.B: But I tell you, a man who looks at a woman with the aim of wanting her for himself has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
en.R: But I tell you, if a man looks at a woman and wants to have sex with her, he has already sinned with her in his heart. It is the same as adultery.

decisions.choice: in order to desire her: looking with the purpose of wanting her sexually
alternatives: noticing that a woman is attractive
decisions.reason: The construction states a purpose. The verb is the one used in the command against coveting a neighbor's wife (Exodus 20:17 in the Greek Old Testament).

decisions.choice: in his heart: in his inner self, where intentions are formed
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the center of thought and will. Sin begins there before it is done (15:19).

decisions.choice: everyone who looks: a man, as the following "his heart" shows
decisions.reason: The saying is put in terms of a man looking at a woman, the case the commandment has in view. The principle applies to all.

decisions.choice: a man who (B); if a man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the saying is about a man; it takes no gender setting.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.

records.literal_gloss: If but the eye of you the right causes to stumble you, tear out it and throw from you; it is better for you that perishes one of the members of you and not whole the body of you be thrown into Gehenna.

en.L: And if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw [it] away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
en.B: If your right eye leads you into sin, pull it out and get rid of it. You are better off losing one part of your body than having all of you thrown into hell.
en.R: If your right eye makes you sin, pull it out and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body thrown into hell.

decisions.choice: tear out, cut off: overstatement that demands drastic action against sin
alternatives: a command to harm the body
decisions.reason: Jesus uses deliberate overstatement, as teachers of the time did. Removing an eye would not stop desire, which comes from the heart (5:28; 15:19). The point is to deal ruthlessly with whatever leads to sin, because the stakes are eternal.

decisions.choice: causes you to stumble: leads you into sin
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a trap or a stone that trips someone. Here it means leading into sin that ruins a person.

decisions.choice: the right eye: the one thought more valuable
decisions.reason: The right eye and the right hand (5:30) were thought the better ones. Even what is most valued must go.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, explained at 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: leads you into sin (B); makes you sin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

source.text: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And if the right of you hand causes to stumble you, cut off it and throw from you; it is better for you that perishes one of the members of you and not whole the body of you into Gehenna go away.

en.L: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw [it] away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.
en.B: And if your right hand leads you into sin, cut it off and get rid of it. You are better off losing one part of your body than having all of you go into hell.
en.R: If your right hand makes you sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go to hell.

decisions.choice: tear out, cut off: overstatement that demands drastic action against sin
alternatives: a command to harm the body
decisions.reason: Jesus uses deliberate overstatement, as teachers of the time did. Removing an eye would not stop desire, which comes from the heart (5:28; 15:19). The point is to deal ruthlessly with whatever leads to sin, because the stakes are eternal.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, explained at 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: leads you into sin (B); makes you sin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:29.

source.text: Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.

records.literal_gloss: It was said also, Whoever divorces the wife of him, let him give to her a certificate of divorce.

en.L: And it was said, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.'
en.B: It was also said, 'A man who sends his wife away must give her a written notice of divorce.'
en.R: The law also says, 'If a man divorces his wife, he must give her a paper that says she is divorced.'

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 24:1-4: the written notice of divorce
decisions.reason: The law took divorce for granted and regulated it: a husband who sent his wife away had to give her a written document, which left her free to marry again.

decisions.choice: divorces: in Jewish law only the husband could divorce
decisions.reason: Teachers of the time disagreed over the grounds. Some allowed divorce only for sexual unfaithfulness, others for almost any cause (19:3).

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.

records.literal_gloss: I but say to you that everyone divorcing the wife of him except on account of sexual immorality makes her to commit adultery, and whoever a divorced [woman] marries commits adultery.

en.L: But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
en.B: But I tell you that a man who divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual unfaithfulness causes her to commit adultery, and anyone who marries a woman who has been divorced commits adultery.
en.R: But I tell you, if a man divorces his wife for any reason except sexual unfaithfulness, he causes her to commit adultery if she marries again. And any man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual unfaithfulness by the wife
decisions.reason: The word covers sexual sin of many kinds. In a saying about marriage it most likely means the wife's unfaithfulness. Others limit it to marriages the law forbade (Leviticus 18) or to unfaithfulness during betrothal (as in 1:19).

decisions.choice: makes her commit adultery: when she marries again, as she would be expected to
alternatives: makes her an adulteress at the moment of divorce
decisions.reason: A divorced woman with no means of support would usually remarry. Since in God's sight the first marriage still stands, that marriage is adultery, and the husband who divorced her bears the blame.

decisions.choice: if she marries again
decisions.reason: Readable states the assumption the saying makes.

source.text: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.

records.literal_gloss: Again you heard that it was said to the ancients, Not you will swear falsely, you will pay but to the Lord the oaths of you.

en.L: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not swear falsely, but you shall carry out your oaths to the Lord.'
en.B: You have also heard what our ancestors were told: 'Do not swear falsely. Do what you have promised the Lord with an oath.'
en.R: You have also heard that people long ago were told, 'Do not make a promise to God and then break it. Do what you promised the Lord.'

decisions.choice: Leviticus 19:12; Numbers 30:2; Deuteronomy 23:21
decisions.reason: The words sum up several laws: do not swear falsely by God's name, and keep the vows you make to him.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew of these laws
decisions.reason: As in 4:7 and 4:10.

decisions.choice: swear falsely: break an oath, or swear to what is untrue
decisions.reason: An oath called on God as witness. The verb covers both false oaths and broken ones.

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: As in 5:21.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: I but say to you not to swear at all; neither by the heaven, because throne it is of the God;

en.L: But I say to you not to swear at all: neither by heaven, because it is [the] throne of God,
en.B: But I tell you, do not take an oath at all, not by heaven, because it is God's throne,
en.R: But I tell you, never make a promise by swearing an oath. Do not swear by heaven, because heaven is where God rules as king.

decisions.choice: not to swear at all: no oaths to guarantee your words
alternatives: no oaths in a law court
decisions.reason: Jesus forbids the oaths people used to make their words believed. Where every word is true, no oath is needed (5:37). Christians have differed over whether this rules out oaths required by a court.

decisions.choice: heaven is God's throne: Isaiah 66:1
decisions.reason: God says, "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool." To swear by heaven is still to swear by God (23:22).

decisions.choice: where God rules as king
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of a throne.

source.text: μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·

records.literal_gloss: nor by the earth, because footstool it is of the feet of him; nor to Jerusalem, because city it is of the great King;

en.L: nor by the earth, because it is [the] footstool of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, nor by Jerusalem, because it is [the] city of the great King,
en.B: or by the earth, because it is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} footstool, or by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.
en.R: Do not swear by the earth, because it belongs to God. It is where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rests {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. Do not swear by Jerusalem, because it is the city of God, the great King.

decisions.choice: footstool: Isaiah 66:1; city of the great King: Psalm 48:2
decisions.reason: The earth and Jerusalem belong to God as much as heaven does. People swore by them to avoid naming God, but every such oath still calls on him.

decisions.choice: it belongs to God; the city of God, the great King
alternatives: his footstool; the city of the great King
decisions.reason: Readable says that each picture speaks of God.

source.text: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.

records.literal_gloss: Nor by the head of you swear, because not you are able one hair white to make or black.

en.L: Nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
en.B: Do not swear by your own head either, since you cannot turn a single hair white or black.
en.R: Do not even swear by your own head. You cannot make one hair on it white or black.

decisions.choice: you cannot make one hair white or black: even your own life is in God's hands
decisions.reason: To swear by one's head was to pledge one's life. But a person does not control even the color of a hair; life belongs to God.

source.text: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Let be but the word of you yes yes, no no; the but more of these from the evil is.

en.L: But let your word be 'Yes, yes,' 'No, no'; and what is more than these is from the evil one.
en.B: Let your yes be yes and your no be no. Whatever you add to that comes from the evil one.
en.R: When you say yes, mean yes. When you say no, mean no. If you say more than that, it comes from the evil one.

decisions.choice: yes, yes; no, no: a plain yes or no that can be trusted
alternatives: a double yes as a kind of oath
decisions.reason: The doubled words stress that a yes should mean yes and a no mean no (compare James 5:12).

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: The form can be masculine (the evil one) or neuter (evil). Matthew uses the masculine of the devil in 13:19 and 13:38, and the need for oaths comes from a world where lying is common.
